### 1. Case Header, Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Concise Recognizable Title:** Soliven v. Makasiar (The Presidential Libel Suit & Immunity Case)
**Full Official Caption:** Maximo V. Soliven, Antonio V. Roces, Frederick K. Agcaoili, and Godofredo L. Manzanas, Petitioners, vs. The Hon. Ramon P. Makasiar, Presiding Judge of the Regional Trial Court of Manila, Branch 35, Undersecretary Silvestre Bello III, of the Department of Justice, Luis C. Victor, The City Fiscal of Manila, and President Corazon C. Aquino, Respondents (G.R. No. L-82585); Luis D. Beltran, Petitioner, vs. The Hon. Ramon P. Makasiar, Presiding Judge of Branch 35 of the Regional Trial Court, at Manila, The Hon. Luis Victor, City Fiscal of Manila, People of the Philippines, Superintendent of the Western Police District, and the Members of the Process Serving Unit at the Regional Trial Court of Manila, Respondents (G.R. No. L-82827); Luis D. Beltran, Petitioner, vs. Executive Secretary Catalino Macaraig, Secretary of Justice Sedfrey Ordoñez, Undersecretary of Justice Silvestre Bello III, The City Fiscal of Manila Jesus F. Guerrero, and Judge Ramon P. Makasiar, Presiding Judge of Branch 35 of the Regional Trial Court, at Manila, Respondents (G.R. No. L-83979).
**Citation & Metadata:** 249 Phil. 394; G.R. Nos. L-82585, L-82827, and L-83979; Promulgated November 14, 1988; En Banc; **Per Curiam**; Concurring Opinion by Gutierrez, Jr., J.
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Luis D. Beltran:** Columnist for the **Philippine Star**, petitioner accused of criminal libel for writing that President Corazon C. Aquino hid under her bed during an attempted military coup.
**Maximo V. Soliven, Antonio V. Roces, Frederick K. Agcaoili, and Godofredo L. Manzanas:** Publisher/Chairman of the Editorial Board, Managing Editor, and Business Managers/Executives of the **Philippine Star**, co-petitioners charged with criminal libel.
**President Corazon C. Aquino:** Incumbent President of the Philippines; private complainant who executed the complaint-affidavit for criminal libel against the columnists and editors.
**Hon. Ramon P. Makasiar:** Presiding Judge, Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Manila, Branch 35, who evaluated the fiscal's information and issued warrants of arrest against petitioners.
**Sedfrey Ordoñez & Silvestre Bello III:** Secretary and Undersecretary of the Department of Justice (DOJ), respectively, who reviewed and sustained the City Fiscal's finding of probable cause.
**Catalino Macaraig:** Executive Secretary, who affirmed the DOJ resolution upon presidential administrative appeal.
**Luis C. Victor & Jesus F. Guerrero:** City Fiscals of Manila who conducted the preliminary investigation and filed the criminal informations for libel.
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:**
Petitions for Certiorari and Prohibition under Rule 65 of the Rules of Court seeking to annul the criminal informations for libel, quash the warrants of arrest issued by RTC Manila Branch 35, and enjoin public respondents from proceeding with the prosecution, on grounds of denial of administrative due process, violation of the constitutional requirements for issuing warrants of arrest, and presidential disability to initiate criminal suits due to presidential immunity from suit.
### 2. Syllabus Topic Grouping, Codal Provision & Factual Trigger
**Primary Topic Hierarchy:**
Constitutional Law I → The Executive Department → Executive Immunities and Privileges → **Presidential Immunity from Suit (Scope, Nature, and Waiver)**
**Secondary Topic Hierarchy:**
Constitutional Law I → Bill of Rights → Searches and Seizures → **Personal Determination of Probable Cause by a Judge for the Issuance of Warrants of Arrest** (Art. III, Sec. 2)
**Full Text of Governing Constitutional / Statutory Provisions:**
**Article III, Section 2, 1987 Constitution of the Philippines:**
"The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures of whatever nature and for any purpose shall be inviolable, and no search warrant or warrant of arrest shall issue except upon probable cause to be determined **personally by the judge after examination under oath or affirmation of the complainant and the witnesses he may produce**, and particularly describing the place to be searched and the persons or things to be seized."
**Historical & Jurisprudential Context of Presidential Immunity:**
Unlike the 1973 Constitution (Art. VII, Sec. 17), which explicitly stated: **"The President shall be immune from suit during his tenure; thereafter, no suit whatsoever shall lie for official acts done by him or by others pursuant to his specific orders during his tenure,"** the 1987 Constitution contains no express codal provision guaranteeing presidential immunity. Under the 1987 Constitution, presidential immunity is maintained as a fundamental doctrine of constitutional common law and structural executive independence, rooted in the separation of powers and the doctrine recognized in **Soliven v. Makasiar**:
**"The rationale for the grant to the President of the privilege of immunity from suit is to assure the exercise of Presidential duties and functions free from any hindrance or distraction, considering that being the Chief Executive of the Government is a job that, aside from requiring all of the office holder's time, also demands undivided attention."**
**Factual Trigger (Application to the Story):**
Following the August 1987 coup attempt, newspaper columnist Luis Beltran wrote a column in the **Philippine Star** alleging that President Corazon Aquino hid under her bed while Malacañang was under siege. Deeply aggrieved, President Aquino initiated a criminal complaint for libel against Beltran, Soliven, and their editors; when RTC Judge Makasiar issued a warrant of arrest based on the fiscal's recommendation, Beltran challenged the proceedings, arguing that because the President enjoys absolute immunity from suit, she suffers an identical "correlative disability" that bars her from instituting a criminal complaint in court.

**Full Official Caption:** Republic of the Philippines, represented by Solicitor General Jose C. Calida, Petitioner, v. Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno, Respondent.
**Citation & Metadata:** G.R. No. 237428; May 11, 2018; 831 Phil. 271; En Banc; Ponente: Associate Justice Noel Gimenez Tijam.
**Voting Breakdown:**
Concurring (8): Tijam (Ponente), Leonardo-De Castro, Peralta, Bersamin, Jardeleza, Martires, A. Reyes, Jr., Gesmundo.
Concurring and Dissenting / Separate Opinions (2): Velasco, Jr., Del Castillo.
Dissenting (4): Carpio, Perlas-Bernabe, Leonen, Caguioa.
Inhibited/No Part (1): Sereno (Respondent).
Separate Opinions Filed: Dissenting Opinions by Carpio, Leonen, Caguioa; Concurring and Dissenting Opinions by Velasco, Jr., Del Castillo; Concurring Opinions by Leonardo-De Castro, Bersamin; Separate Concurring Opinion by Peralta; Separate Opinions by Perlas-Bernabe, Martires.
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Petitioner:** Republic of the Philippines, represented by Solicitor General Jose C. Calida, invoking the sovereign right of the State to institute **quo warranto** proceedings against an allegedly unqualified occupant of a public office.
**Respondent:** Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno, incumbent Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines, whose title and qualifications are directly challenged.
**Judicial and Bar Council (JBC):** The constitutionally mandated body tasked with screening and nominating applicants to judicial vacancies, operating under the supervisory authority of the Supreme Court.
**University of the Philippines (UP) / UP College of Law / UP HRDO:** Respondent’s former public employer (faculty member from 1986 to 2006) whose human resource and custodian records established the missing Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).
**Office of the Ombudsman:** The constitutional repository agency of public officials' SALNs that issued official certifications regarding respondent’s unfiled SALNs.
**Movant-Intervenors:** Groups of citizens, taxpayers, organizations, and legislators—including Capistrano **et al.**, Zarate **et al.**, the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), and Senators Leila De Lima and Antonio Trillanes IV—seeking intervention to dismiss the petition.
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:** Direct invocation of the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Section 5(1), Article VIII of the 1987 Constitution in relation to Rule 66 of the Rules of Court (Special Civil Action for **Quo Warranto**), commenced by the Republic through the Solicitor General following letter-requests and disclosures made during House Committee on Justice impeachment proceedings.

**Citation & Metadata:** G.R. No. 164195; April 30, 2008; 576 Phil. 234; Third Division; Ponente: Chico-Nazario, J.; Voting: Unanimous (Ynares-Santiago, **J., Chairperson**, Austria-Martinez, Nachura, and Reyes, **JJ.**, concurring).

**Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP):** Government financial intermediary and agrarian financial institution tasked with land valuation and compensation disbursement under CARP; Private Respondent.

- Gesmundo, C.J., Hernando, Inting, Zalameda, M. Lopez, Gaerlan, Rosario, J. Lopez, Dimaampao, and Marquez, JJ., concurred.

### 1. Case Header, Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Concise Recognizable Title:** Re: Draft DOJ-NPS Rules on Preliminary Investigations and Inquest Proceedings
**Full Official Caption:** Re: Draft Department of Justice-National Prosecution Service's [DOJ-NPS] Rules on Preliminary Investigations and Inquest Proceedings
**Citation & Metadata:** A.M. No. 24-02-09-SC; May 28, 2024; 955 Phil. 15; En Banc; Zalameda, **J.** (Voting: Unanimous; Gesmundo, **C.J.**, Leonen, **SAJ.**, Caguioa, Hernando, Lazaro-Javier, Inting, M. Lopez, Gaerlan, Rosario, J. Lopez, Dimaampao, Marquez, Kho, Jr., and Singh, **JJ.**, concur; No separate opinions filed).
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
** Supreme Court of the Philippines (**En Banc) – The constitutional organ vested with exclusive rule-making authority over pleading, practice, and procedure in all courts.
Sub-Committee on the Revision of the Rules of Criminal Procedure (Sub-Committee) – Chaired by Associate Justice Rodil V. Zalameda, tasked with revising Rule 112 of the Rules of Court.
Department of Justice (DOJ) / National Prosecution Service (NPS) – Executive department led by Secretary of Justice; represented in discussions by Undersecretary Raul T. Vasquez; drafted executive rules governing executive preliminary investigations and inquest proceedings.
Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo – Chief Justice of the Philippines; initiated transmittal of Court comments and proposed the formal recognition of DOJ's executive rule-making power and the corresponding repeal of inconsistent provisions in Rule 112.
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:**
This administrative matter originated internally upon transmittal by a DOJ member of the draft Department Circular containing the proposed **Rules on Preliminary Investigations and Inquest Proceedings in the National Prosecution Service** (DOJ-NPS Rules) to the Court's Sub-Committee on the Revision of the Rules of Criminal Procedure. The Court resolved **en banc** whether to recognize the DOJ's authority to promulgate executive rules on preliminary investigations and inquest proceedings, and whether to repeal the corresponding provisions in Rule 112 of the 2000 Revised Rules of Criminal Procedure.

**Concise Recognizable Title: In Re: Cunanan (The Bar Flunkers’ Case)**
**Full Official Caption:** In the Matter of the Petitions for Admission to the Bar of Unsuccessful Candidates of 1946 to 1953; Albino Cunanan et al., Petitioners
**Citation & Metadata:** 94 Phil. 534; En Banc Resolution Promulgated March 18, 1954; Ponente: Diokno, J.
**Voting Breakdown:** Concurring with the main opinion: Bengzon, Montemayor, Jugo, Labrador, Pablo, Padilla, and Reyes, JJ. (Justice Labrador filed an additional concurring/dissenting opinion voting to strike down the entire Act; Chief Justice Paras filed a separate concurring/dissenting opinion voting to uphold the Act in its entirety; two Justices did not take part in voting).
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Albino Cunanan et al.:** Petitioners; unsuccessful postwar Philippine Bar candidates (examinations from 1946 to 1953) seeking admission to the Bar under Republic Act No. 972 or via motions for grade reconsideration.
**Juan R. Liwag:** Solicitor General of the Philippines, appearing as amicus curiae/respondent contesting the constitutionality of Republic Act No. 972.
**Congress of the Philippines:** Legislative body that enacted Republic Act No. 972 over the known objections of the Supreme Court.
**Jose M. Aruego, M. H. de Joya, Miguel R. Cornejo, Antonio Enrile Inton, E. Voltaire Garcia, Vicente J. Francisco, Vicente Pelaez, and Buenaventura Evangelista:** Counsel and amici curiae advocating for petitioners and defending the validity of Republic Act No. 972.
**U.P. Women Lawyers’ Circle, Arturo A. Alafriz, Enrique M. Fernando, Vicente Abad Santos, Carlos A. Barrios, Vicente del Rosario, Juan de Blancaflor, Mamerto V. Gonzales, and Roman Ozaeta:** Bar organizations, counsel, and amici curiae arguing against the validity of Republic Act No. 972.
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:**
Original ex parte mass and individual petitions filed directly before the Supreme Court by unsuccessful postwar Bar examinees praying for admission to the Bar and permission to take the lawyer's oath pursuant to Republic Act No. 972, joined with pending and resolved motions for grade reconsideration. Entertaining grave doubts regarding the law's validity, the Supreme Court set the petitions for hearing exclusively on the constitutionality of Republic Act No. 972.

**Full Official Caption:** Enrique A. Zaldivar, Petitioner, v. The Honorable Sandiganbayan and Honorable Raul M. Gonzalez, claiming to be and acting as Tanodbayan-Ombudsman under the 1987 Constitution, Respondents (G.R. Nos. L-79690-707); Enrique A. Zaldivar, Petitioner, v. Hon. Raul M. Gonzalez, claiming to be and acting as Tanodbayan-Ombudsman under the 1987 Constitution, Respondent (G.R. No. L-80578).
**Citation & Metadata:** G.R. Nos. L-79690-707 & G.R. No. L-80578; Promulgated October 7, 1988; 248 Phil. 542; **Per Curiam**; En Banc (Concurring: Fernan, C.J., Narvasa, Melencio-Herrera, Gutierrez, Jr., Cruz, Paras, Feliciano, Gancayco, Padilla, Bidin, Sarmiento, Cortes, Griño-Aquino, Medialdea, and Regalado, JJ.; no separate opinions filed).

**Enrique A. Zaldivar:** Petitioner; Governor of Antique, charged with multiple violations of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act before the Sandiganbayan.

### 1. Case Header, Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Concise Recognizable Title: Vargas v. Rilloraza** (The People's Court Collaboration Disqualification Case)
**Full Official Caption:** Jorge B. Vargas, Petitioner, v. Emilio Rilloraza, Jose Bernabe, Manuel Escudero, Judges of the People's Court, and The Solicitor General of the Philippines, Respondents.
**Citation & Metadata:** G.R. No. L-1612; Promulgated February 26, 1948; 80 Phil. 297; Ponente: Hilado, J.; En Banc. Voting Breakdown: Hilado, J., ponente, joined by Moran, C.J. (with separate concurring opinion), Paras, Pablo, Bengzon, and Tuason, JJ.; Perfecto, J. (concurring with separate opinion); Briones, J. (concurring in the result/fallo).
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Jorge B. Vargas:** Petitioner; accused collaborator indicted for treason before the People's Court for having occupied prominent executive positions (such as Chairman of the Philippine Executive Commission) during the Japanese military occupation.
**Emilio Rilloraza, Jose Bernabe, and Manuel Escudero:** Respondents; Associate Judges of the People's Court presiding over petitioner's prosecution.
**The Solicitor General of the Philippines (Manuel Lim, assisted by Assistant Solicitor General Manuel P. Barcelona):** Respondent public prosecutor representing the Commonwealth/Republic government in prosecuting treason cases.
**Claro M. Recto:** Counsel for petitioner Jorge B. Vargas.
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:** Direct constitutional challenge raised via Motion dated August 28, 1947, in an original petition/proceeding before the Supreme Court, formally assailing the constitutionality of Section 14 of Commonwealth Act No. 682 (The People's Court Act), which disqualified certain Supreme Court Justices from hearing collaboration treason appeals and authorized the President to designate temporary substitute Justices from inferior courts.
